description: JACL Milestone 2 — Parser & AST: Recursive descent parser producing arena-allocated AST from lexer token stream, with panic mode error recovery, source positions on all nodes, and round-trip pretty-printer

userStories.title: Define AST node types and structures
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need a well-defined set of AST node types so that I can pattern-match on nodes during bytecode compilation.
acceptanceCriteria: parser/ast.h exists following single-header convention (#ifndef AST_H / #define AST_H for declarations, #ifdef AST_IMPLEMENTATION for implementation)
AstNodeType enum covers: AST_COMMAND, AST_LIT_INT, AST_LIT_FLOAT, AST_LIT_STRING, AST_VAR_REF, AST_BLOCK, AST_INTERP_STRING, AST_ERROR
SourcePos struct with fields: uint32_t line, uint32_t column, uint32_t offset
AstNode struct is a tagged union: AstNodeType type field, SourcePos start and SourcePos end fields, union of type-specific data
AST_COMMAND data: AstNode* head (first child is command name node), AstNode** args, uint32_t arg_count
AST_LIT_INT data: int32_t value
AST_LIT_FLOAT data: float value
AST_LIT_STRING data: const char* value, uint32_t length
AST_VAR_REF data: const char* name, uint32_t length
AST_BLOCK data: AstNode** commands, uint32_t count
AST_INTERP_STRING data: AstNode** segments, uint32_t count (segments are string literals, var refs, or commands)
AST_ERROR data: const char* message
All AstNode structs are arena-allocated — no individual free required
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Define ParseResult and parser API
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need a parser entry point that accepts lexer output and returns a structured parse result so that compilation can begin from AST.
acceptanceCriteria: parser/parser.h exists following single-header convention (#ifndef PARSER_H / #define PARSER_H for declarations, #ifdef PARSER_IMPLEMENTATION for implementation)
parser.h includes lexer/lexer.h and parser/ast.h
ParseResult struct with fields: AstNode** nodes (array of top-level AST nodes), uint32_t count (number of top-level nodes), uint32_t error_count (number of parse errors)
Public API: ParseResult parser_parse(LexResult tokens, arena_t* arena)
parser/test_parser.c exists with test scaffolding using test/test_helpers.h and tracked_allocator
Test file uses table-driven main() pattern matching lexer test style
Test entry added to build.sh TESTS array
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Parse literal values
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need literal AST nodes so that constant values can be loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: TOKEN_INT (42, 0xFF, 0b1010) produces AST_LIT_INT node with correct int32_t value
TOKEN_FLOAT (3.14) produces AST_LIT_FLOAT node with correct float value
TOKEN_WORD (bare words like hello, foo) produces AST_LIT_STRING node
TOKEN_STRING ("hello") produces AST_LIT_STRING node with decoded string content
Source positions (start and end) are correct on every literal node
Tests verify each literal type with correct values and positions
All tests pass and no memory leaks detected by tracked allocator

userStories.title: Parse variable references
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need variable reference AST nodes so that $var can compile to variable lookups.
acceptanceCriteria: TOKEN_VAR ($identifier) produces AST_VAR_REF node with the identifier name (without $)
Variable references work as standalone expressions parsed in argument positions
Source position span includes the $ prefix
Tests verify $x, $foo, $long_name produce correct var ref nodes
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse bracketed command invocations
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need command invocation AST nodes so that [cmd arg1 arg2] compiles to call sequences.
acceptanceCriteria: [cmd arg1 arg2] produces AST_COMMAND with head=string('cmd'), args=[string('arg1'), string('arg2')]
[+ 1 2] produces AST_COMMAND with head=string('+'), args=[int(1), int(2)]
Nested: [print [+ 1 2]] produces command whose second child is another command node
Deep nesting: [a [b [c 1]]] produces correct three-level tree
Variable args: [print $x] produces command with var_ref argument
Empty brackets [] produce a parse error (AST_ERROR node)
Mismatched bracket [cmd arg produces a parse error with source position
Source positions span from opening [ to closing ]
Tests verify all above cases with correct AST structure
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse top-level bare commands
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need top-level bare commands parsed with implicit brackets so that users can write 'print hello' instead of '[print hello]'.
acceptanceCriteria: 'print hello world' at top level produces AST_COMMAND equivalent to [print hello world]
Newlines delimit commands: 'print a\nprint b' produces two separate command nodes
Semicolons delimit commands: 'print a; print b' produces two separate command nodes
Blank lines (consecutive newlines) are skipped — no empty commands produced
Nested brackets in bare commands: 'print [+ 1 2]' produces [print [+ 1 2]]
Variable refs in bare commands: 'print $x' produces [print $x]
A single bare word 'foo' produces a command with no arguments
Source positions span from first token to last token of the bare command
Tests verify all above cases
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse code blocks
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need code block AST nodes so that { ... } arguments to builtins like proc and if can be compiled.
acceptanceCriteria: { print hello } produces AST_BLOCK containing one command
Multi-line blocks: newline-delimited commands within braces produce block with multiple commands
Semicolons within blocks: { print a; print b } produces block with two commands
Blocks as command arguments: [if $cond { print yes } { print no }] parses correctly with two block arguments
Nested blocks: { if $x { inner } } parses with correct nesting
Empty block {} produces AST_BLOCK with zero commands
Mismatched brace { cmd produces a parse error with position info
Source positions span from { to }
Tests verify all above cases
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse string interpolation
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need interpolated string AST nodes so that "hello $name" compiles to string concatenation.
acceptanceCriteria: Non-interpolated "hello" produces plain AST_LIT_STRING node (not interp string)
"hello $name" produces AST_INTERP_STRING with segments: [string('hello '), var_ref('name')]
"result: $[+ 1 2]" produces AST_INTERP_STRING with segments: [string('result: '), command(+ 1 2)]
Multiple interpolations: "$a and $b" produces correct segment sequence
Adjacent interpolations: "$a$b" produces correct structure
Source positions cover full string including quotes
Tests verify all above cases
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse complete multi-line programs
userStories.description: As the compiler, I need to parse complete multi-line JACL programs into a list of top-level AST nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-line program produces a ParseResult with correct array of top-level command nodes
Mixed syntax: bare commands, bracketed commands, and commands with block arguments coexist correctly
A realistic program (10+ lines mixing def, proc, if, arithmetic) parses into correct AST
Empty input produces ParseResult with count=0, error_count=0
Comment-only input produces ParseResult with count=0, error_count=0
Source positions correct across many lines
Tests include at least one integration test with a full multi-construct program
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: Parse error recovery with panic mode
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the parser to recover from errors and continue parsing so that multiple issues are reported at once.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing closing bracket [print hello produces AST_ERROR and parsing continues to next top-level command
Missing closing brace { print hello produces AST_ERROR and parsing continues
Unexpected token (e.g., ] at top level) produces AST_ERROR and parsing continues
Multiple errors in one program all produce error nodes with source positions and descriptive messages
ParseResult.error_count reflects the total number of errors
Panic mode: on error inside [...], parser skips to matching ] (tracking bracket depth); on error inside {...}, skips to matching }; at top level, skips to next newline or EOF
Valid code after errors still parses correctly
Tests verify: single error recovery, multiple errors, errors interleaved with valid code
All tests pass and no memory leaks

userStories.title: AST pretty-printer for round-trip verification
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an AST pretty-printer so that I can verify parse correctness via round-trip testing.
acceptanceCriteria: ast_pretty_print function takes an AstNode* and an arena_t*, returns a const char* (arena-allocated string)
ast_pretty_print_program function takes AstNode** nodes, uint32_t count, and arena_t*, returns const char* with newline-separated commands
Commands print in explicit bracket form: [cmd arg1 arg2]
Literals print as source representation: 42, 3.14, hello
Variable references print as $name
Code blocks print as { cmd1; cmd2 }
Interpolated strings print as "segment $var segment $[cmd] segment"
Round-trip: parsing the pretty-printed output of any valid input produces a structurally equivalent AST
Tests verify round-trip for at least 5 different inputs covering all node types
All tests pass and no memory leaks
